newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN says Iraqi oil pricing formula not approved.
newsitem.headline: UN says Iraqi oil pricing formula not approved.

text.p: A U.N. official said on Friday that a pricing formula for oil sale contracts under the Iraqi oil-for-food deal had not been approved yet because of objections from one Security Council member.

Chinmaya Gharekhan, an undersecretary-general and adviser to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, said there was an objection from one country he did not identify but which one source indicated was the United States.

Gharekhan described the objection as a "highly technical one" rather than political and suggested there had not been enough time yet for the Security Council's sanctions committee to consider the formula.

The committee received the pricing mechanism on Tuesday and gave members two days to review it under its so-called "no objection" procedure. This meant the formula would have been automatically accepted unless a member objected.
Details of the pricing formula were not available but diplomats said earlier it called for the price of Iraqi oil to be tied to benchmark crudes, including Brent, Dubai and West Texas Intermediate.

The formula was worked out over the past two weeks between officials from Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) and oil experts or overseers hired by the United Nations, who will monitor the future oil contracts.

Aside from the pricing formula, the oil-for-food deal has been delayed because of the crisis in Iraq when Baghdad's troops moved into Kurdish areas in the north and the United States retaliated by firing cruise missile.

The plan, signed between the United Nations and Iraq, calls for Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other necessities for its people to ease the impact of six years of U.N. trade sanctions.
